The Program Manager will work closely with senior technical staff at GHSD headquarters, U.S. Embassies, partner governments, implementing partners, and other stakeholders. The Program Manager will help keep HIV programs organized, well documented, and on schedule. This role suits an early to mid-career public health professional who has strong administrative and organizational skills, learns quickly, and cares about global health. Support senior technical staff in giving country teams and partner governments technical assistance on HIV prevention, care, and treatment. This includes organizing meetings, preparing materials, taking notes, and tracking follow-up actions. Support Grants Officer Representatives on HIV and other health-related awards. This includes tracking deliverables, deadlines, budgets, and reporting requirements. Maintain organized program files, award documentation, trackers, and databases so information stays accurate and easy to access. Collect, organize, and summarize program performance data against established metrics and milestones. Help identify trends, gaps, and potential risks. Help draft, edit, and format technical guidance, tools, training materials, and other resources for HIV programs and award management. Coordinate logistics and communications with U.S. Embassies, Ministries of Health, implementing partners, and other stakeholders, including scheduling, correspondence, meeting preparation, and follow-up. Research and summarize relevant literature, program documents, and global health developments to inform team decisions. Help document and share lessons learned and effective practices. Draft and formatted technical guidance documents, tools, and training materials, prepared under the direction of senior staff. Meeting agendas, notes, action-item trackers, and logistics plans for project meetings and stakeholder engagements. Draft inputs to Congressional reports, leadership briefings, and related reporting products, submitted on required timelines. Research summaries and background materials on HIV and global health topics. Regular progress reports detailing achievements, challenges, lessons learned, and recommendations. Foundational knowledge of public health principles and global health issues, including a strong understanding of HIV prevention, care, and treatment. Ability to learn new subject matter, systems, and processes quickly and apply them independently. Strong written communication skills, including drafting, editing, summarizing, and formatting professional documents. Experience in program support, project coordination, or administrative management is strongly preferred. Prior experience working in global health or HIV (including internships, fellowships, practicums, or academic projects) are desired. Work Schedule: Position is full-time, 40 hours per week (Monday-Friday) in Washington, DC. Travel: Up to 25%.
